title: Born in Lahore, Punjab
description: Aslam Hayat was born on 23 March 1933 in Lahore, Punjab, with family roots in Subhan Pur, Kapurthala, Punjab — a life that would span nine decades and cross four continents.

title: Witnessed the Partition of India
description: Aslam Hayat was fourteen years old when the Partition of India reshaped the subcontinent. The historic events he witnessed in Lahore remained an important part of his personal memories throughout his life and informed much of his later writing on history and identity.

title: Muslim Model High School, Lahore
description: Aslam Hayat completed his school education at Muslim Model High School in Lahore — one of the oldest and most distinguished schools in the city.

title: Voyage to London by Sea
description: In the mid-1950s, Aslam Hayat made his first overseas journey — a voyage by sea from Pakistan to England to pursue professional accountancy studies in London. He passed through the Strait of Gibraltar and saw the coast of Tangier, Morocco from the vessel. He spoke of this journey throughout his life as one of the defining experiences of his early years.
location: London, United Kingdom (via Strait of Gibraltar)

title: Qualified as Chartered Accountant, London
description: Aslam Hayat qualified as a Chartered Accountant in London in the late 1950s to early 1960s — a professional achievement that formed the foundation of his subsequent three-decade career in civil aviation. His years in London also exposed him to international journalism, world literature, and ideas that remained with him for life.

title: Joined Pakistan Civil Aviation
description: Following his return from London, Aslam Hayat joined the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority — beginning a distinguished career in public service that would span more than two decades.

title: Posted in Karachi — First Decade of Service
description: Aslam Hayat was posted in Karachi for more than a decade during the 1960s and 1970s. During this period he participated in the growth and modernisation of Pakistan's aviation sector while developing extensive professional experience in civil aviation administration.

title: Transferred to Islamabad — Senior Leadership
description: In the 1970s and 1980s, Aslam Hayat was transferred to Islamabad where he served in increasingly senior management and leadership positions within the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority, ultimately rising to director-level responsibilities.

title: Retired from Public Service
description: After more than two decades of distinguished service in civil aviation administration, Aslam Hayat retired from the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority in Lahore. His career was marked by dedication, integrity, and a lifelong commitment to public service.

title: Immigrated to Vancouver, Canada
description: In 1989, Aslam Hayat immigrated to Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada — beginning a new chapter centred on family, writing, scholarship, community involvement, and lifelong learning. He left behind the life he had built in Pakistan so that future generations could have opportunity. He remained in Vancouver for the rest of his life.

title: Columnist at The Miracle Newspaper
description: From the 1990s until 2026, Aslam Hayat published more than 650 articles in The Miracle, Vancouver's Pakistani community newspaper. His writings explored Islam, Sufism, history, current affairs, science, literature, community issues, and personal reflections — a body of work spanning more than twenty-five years.

title: First Hajj Pilgrimage to Makkah
description: In 1993, Aslam Hayat fulfilled the fifth pillar of Islam and completed his first Hajj pilgrimage to Makkah — one of the most important spiritual milestones of his life.

title: Second Hajj Pilgrimage to Makkah
description: In 1997, Aslam Hayat completed his second Hajj pilgrimage to Makkah, deepening a spiritual relationship with the holy cities that would continue through five Umrah pilgrimages in the years that followed.

title: First Umrah Pilgrimage
description: Completed Umrah pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah in 2003 — the first of five Umrah journeys he would make over the following years.

title: Second Umrah Pilgrimage
description: Completed his second Umrah pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah in 2005.

title: Journey to Istanbul, Turkey
description: A major family journey to Istanbul, Turkey with grandson Zeeshan Hayat and family. He visited Topkapi Palace, the Blue Mosque, and the historic sites of Istanbul — and frequently described this as one of his favourite international journeys. Over his lifetime he also travelled to Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, Cyprus, Egypt, France, the United Arab Emirates, Pakistan, and the United States.

title: Third Umrah Pilgrimage
description: Completed his third Umrah pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah in 2010.

title: Fourth Umrah Pilgrimage
description: Completed his fourth Umrah pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah in 2013.

title: Journey to Egypt — Shrine of Imam Hussain
description: In 2017, Aslam Hayat travelled to Egypt, visiting Cairo and the historic shrine associated with Hazrat Imam Hussain. He often spoke about this visit as a profound spiritual experience and considered it an honour to have visited one of the most revered sites in Islamic history.

title: Fifth Umrah Pilgrimage
description: In 2019, Aslam Hayat completed his fifth Umrah pilgrimage to Makkah and Madinah — completing a lifetime of sacred journeys that totalled 2 Hajj pilgrimages and 5 Umrah pilgrimages.

title: Lifelong Student of Knowledge
description: Throughout his life, Aslam Hayat maintained a deep personal library and commitment to learning. He studied Quran and Tafsir, Hadith, Islamic history, Sufism, comparative religion, philosophy, physics, cosmology, world politics, and economics. He read extensively the works of Ibn Arabi, Abdul Qadir Jilani, Imam Al-Ghazali, Jalaluddin Rumi, Data Ganj Bakhsh, Baba Farid, Al-Razi, Kabir Helminski, Karen Armstrong, and Neil Douglas-Klotz.

title: Passed Away in Vancouver, aged 93
description: Aslam Hayat passed away in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada at the age of 93. His legacy continues through his family, his 650+ published articles, his scholarship, and the preservation of his life story in The Aslam Hayat Legacy Archive. إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
